name: Qing dynasty
summary: A blue dragon on a yellow field, reaching toward a red flaming pearl in the upper hoist. The first national flag of China, it was introduced by the Qing dynasty in the late 19th century for diplomacy and shipping.
origin: Imperial China had no national flag until contact with Western navies made one necessary. In 1862 the Qing government introduced a triangular yellow flag with a dragon for naval and diplomatic use.

In 1889 the flag was changed to a rectangle, the form shown here. It was used until the Xinhai Revolution overthrew the dynasty in 1911–1912, after which the Republic of China adopted the five-coloured flag.

colors.name: Yellow
colors.meaning: The colour of the emperor; under the Qing it was reserved for imperial use.

symbols.name: Azure dragon
symbols.description: A blue Chinese dragon with five claws.
symbols.meaning: The emperor; the five-clawed dragon was an imperial emblem.

symbols.name: Flaming pearl
symbols.description: A red disc in the upper hoist, which the dragon reaches for.
symbols.meaning: Commonly explained as the sun, or wisdom and prosperity.

facts: The Republic of China's first flag (1912–1928) had five horizontal stripes for the Han, Manchu, Mongol, Hui and Tibetan peoples.
The Yellow Dragon Flag is one of the few national flags to show a dragon; Bhutan's is another.
Under Qing dress regulations, bright yellow was reserved for the emperor.
clues: A blue dragon on yellow reaching for a red pearl.
The first national flag of a vast empire, created for naval and diplomatic use.
Replaced by a five-stripe flag after a revolution in 1911–1912.
